name: City Council Meeting
minutes_text:
MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  March 3, 2014

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Kelley at 5:02 p.m., on March 3, 2014, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on February 26, 2014, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the
Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Reardon
  Council Member Schlicht (arrived at 5:05 p.m.)
  Council Member Ury (arrived at 5:40 p.m.)
  Mayor Pro Tem Leckness
  Mayor Kelley

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

RECESS

At the hour of 5:02 p.m., Mayor Kelley declared a recess. The City Council reconvened at 6:01
p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Schlicht

INVOCATION: Council Member Ury

City Council Minutes  1  March 3, 2014
 PRESENTATIONS

P1. Proclaim March 2014 To Be "Prescription Drug Abuse Awareness Month"

  Mayor Kelley presented the proclamation to Natalie Costa, Producer of the Documentary
  "Behind the Orange Curtain."

P2. Recognize Tammy Descoteaux for her Years of Service with the Community of
  Character Program

  Mayor Kelley presented a certificate of appreciation to Tammy Descoteaux.

P3. Presentation by the American Cancer Society in Appreciation of the City hosting the
  Cancer Prevention Study - 3

  The City Council received the presentation and plaques from Allison Levy, Orange County
  Community Engagement Representative with the American Cancer Society.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Heidi Tully, M.V. (via email): noted that there is a lack of any restroom facilities at a majority of
the parks used for soccer and other sports and she stated that restrooms are not just a nice
commodity; they are a necessity.

Mary Lee Robinson, M.V.: expressed her gratitude for the additional lights at the Community
Center and she said that she feels safer now because the parking lot is well lit.

Larry Gilbert, M.V.: concurred that there is a need for restrooms at the City parks where sports
are played. He stated that Pavion Park should be split out into its own designation in the City's
budget and he expressed opposition to the cost for the proposed Pavion Park rehabilitation. Mr.
Gilbert asked how much money has already been spent on the project.

Garry Hewitt, Ladera Ranch: asked the City to assist in his research to determine if there is an
issue locally with pinhole/slab leaks in area homes. He provided a letter with information on a
survey that is available for residents to complete on surveymonkey.com.

Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: drew the Council's attention to an article in the LA Times regarding
two fire captains who were reassigned due to alleged favoritism when their sons advanced in the
fire department. He stated that he is certain that the same type of investigation will soon occur at
the OCFA regarding Mayor Kelley's son and he requested that Council Member Reardon or
Council Member Schlicht replace Mayor Kelley on the OCFA Board.

Wendy Bucknum, M.V.: announced that the Elks Club recently held a marathon bingo event and
the proceeds will go to the neurological center at Mission Hospital. She encouraged residents to
participate and submit their chili cook-off applications and to attend "South County's Got Talent"
on March 12. Mrs. Bucknum provided fliers on the event and invited the community to attend.
City Council Minutes  2  March 3, 2014
 CONSENT CALENDAR

Items 4 and 5 were removed from the Consent Calendar for separate discussion.

Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Leckness, to approve the
Consent Calendar as described below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions

  Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said titles
  which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been ready by title and
  further reading waived.

2.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the Regular City Council Meeting of February 17, 2014, as
  presented.

3.  Check Register Dated February 7, 2014 in the Amount of $1,372,676.60

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

PUBLIC HEARINGS

OLD BUSINESS

6.  Amendment to Library Hours for 2014 Calendar Year

  Stephanie Tanton, Director of Library and Cultural Services, presented the staff report.

  Council Member Schlicht expressed some concern with the proposed closure dates and
  stated that she doesn't want the Mission Viejo Library to go below the service levels of the
  County Library.

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Council Member Reardon, to approve
  the Amendment to Library Hours for 2014 Calendar Year.

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Council Member Reardon, to call the
  question.

City Council Minutes  3  March 3, 2014
   On roll call, said motion (to call the question) carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Reardon, and Ury
  NOES:  Leckness and Schlicht
  ABSENT:  None

  On roll call, said MAIN motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT:  None

7.  Selection of the Dog Park Name

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay presented the staff
  report. Mr. Rattay asked the Council to choose the top three names for the dog park and to
  randomly choose a resident's name where there were multiple submissions for the same dog
  park name.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Leckness, seconded by Council Member Ury, to name the
  dog park La Paws Park.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  Reardon
  ABSENT:  None

  Motion made by Council Member Reardon, seconded by Council Member Ury, to award
  2nd place to the name Canine Canyon.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  Leckness
  ABSENT:  None

  Motion made by Council Member Reardon, seconded by Council Member Ury, to award
  3rd place to the name Wiggly Field.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  Leckness
  ABSENT:  None

City Council Minutes  4  March 3, 2014
   For the first place prize (an iPad Mini,) Mayor Pro Tem Leckness randomly chose a name
  from the six submitted for La Paws Park. The winner of the drawing was Teri Armstrong.

  Mayor Kelley announced that there were single submissions for the 2nd and 3rd place dog
  park names so there was no need for a drawing. The winner of the 2nd place prize (an iPod
  Classic) for the name Canine Canyon was Mary Benning, and the 3rd place winner (an
  iPod Shuffle) for the name Wiggly Field Dog Park was Ellie Boone.

NEW BUSINESS

8.  Second Amendment to the Construction and Demolition Waste Recycling Ordinance

  Environmental Programs Administrator Denise Matson presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Leckness, to
  introduce Ordinance 14-302 Amending Paragraph (c) of Section 6.10.1140 of Division 10,
  Chapter 6.10 of Title 6 of the Mission Viejo Municipal Code Relating to the Use of
  Diversion Performance Deposits.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT:  None

9.  Resolution for a 20 Percent Voluntary Reduction in Water Usage

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Leckness, to adopt
  Resolution 14-07 Calling for a 20 Percent Voluntary Reduction in Water Usage by All
  Residence, Commercial Property Owners, Business Owners and Public Facilities Located
  in Mission Viejo.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

4.  Check Register Dated February 14, 2014 in the Amount of $383,411.87

  Council Member Schlicht inquired about a $1,400 payment to the California Association of
  Parks for a March banquet reservation.
City Council Minutes  5  March 3, 2014
   Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas responded that the payment was the
  registration fee for Community Services Commissioners and staff to attend the annual
  Parks and Recreation Society conference next week.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Ury, to ratify the
  accompanying check register.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

5.  CoolCalifornia City Challenge

  Denise Matson, Environmental Programs Administrator, presented the staff report and
  answered the City Council Members questions.

  Council Member Schlicht expressed opposition to the program and said that it perpetuates
  the myth of global warming. She stated that she doesn’t see any benefit for the citizens or
  for the State and she doesn’t know what the company would do with her personal
  information.

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Leckness, to authorize
  the City Manager to submit a letter of support stating the City's commitment to the
  CoolCalifornia City Challenge.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, and Ury
  NOES:  Reardon and Schlicht
  ABSENT:  None

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

10. Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: provided highlights on a variety of issues with the OCFA.

  Mayor Kelley presented the report.

11. Orange County Transportation Authority (OCTA)

  Council Member Ury presented the report.

City Council Minutes  6  March 3, 2014
 STAFF REPORTS

City Manager’s Report

12. Mid-Year Budget Review for FY 2013/14

  Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas presented the staff report and answered the
  City Council Members questions.

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Leckness, to adopt
  Resolution 14-08 Amending the FY 2013/14 Budget for Adjustments to Certain Revenue
  Sources and Operating and Capital Improvement Program Appropriations (removed all
  items related to the Mission Viejo Foundation.)

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, an Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Leckness, to adopt
  Resolution 14-09 Amending the FY 2013-14 Budget for Adjustments to Certain Revenue
  Sources and Operating and Capital Improvement Program Appropriations (approving the
  recommendation to zero out the Mission Viejo Foundation Fund.)

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT:  None

City Manager’s Report (Continued)

City Manager Wilberg informed the Council that Target is no longer sponsoring Pacific
Symphony Orchestra (PSO) and while staff originally thought that there wouldn't be a concert
this summer, they have been discussing the matter with the PSO. Pacific Symphony has agreed
to put on the Mission Viejo concert with a $50,000 commitment from the City. The City has
always provided $30,000 and the Friends of the Mission Viejo Arts have pledged $5,000 so staff
is trying to identify other potential sponsors for the remaining $15,000. Staff will return to the
Council in April and they hope that the City can make a commitment to hold the PSO again this
summer.

Mr. Wilberg shared a presentation that he gave to the South Orange County Economic Coalition
on residential and commercial development activity, road improvements, and CIP projects.

City Council Minutes  7  March 3, 2014
 City Attorney’s Report

City Attorney Curley announced that he had nothing to report.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

13. Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  The City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars as presented
  in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public record.

Council Member Reardon

Council Member Reardon announced that the Mission Viejo Pony League Black Hawk Team,
which won two World Championships in 2012 and 2013, are holding a fundraising golf
tournament on Friday, March 7 at Tijeras Creek Golf Course. She noted that the team is
comprised of a great group of coaches and kids and she encouraged residents to contact her or
James Tyler for more information (949-295-9702 or james@tylerlogistics.com.) Council
Member Reardon congratulated City employees Mark Joson and Raul Villalobos who recently
took advantage of a CSUF Leadership Development Program for public agencies. It was a 10-
month program and Raul presented closing comments describing what the program meant to him
and his classmates. She stated that the City is very proud of these employees for devoting the
time to advance themselves in their careers. Council Member Reardon announced that the movie
Behind the Orange Curtain will be shown on March 19 at 7:00 p.m. at the Casta del Sol
recreation room. It will be open to the public and Natalie Costa, producer of the movie, will be
there with health-care and law enforcement experts to answer questions of the audience. She
also encouraged interested residents to hear Leigh Steinberg, the real life "Jerry Maguire," on
Thursday, March 6, at 7:00 p.m. at the Murray Community Center and she concluded her
comments by recounting her experience watching Son of God, the movie, which she enjoyed
from a historical and relational perspective.

Council Member Schlicht

Council Member Schlicht stated that during agenda item 6, regarding the library closure, Council
Member Ury said that that the library will only closed for two days then he called the question to
stop the discussion. She stated that in truth, the library will be closed for three days yet the
County library system will only close one day during the Christmas break. By calling the
question, there was no further opportunity to address why staff did not follow through with
Council's direction to come back with library attendance numbers. Council Member Schlicht,
referring to agenda item 5, stated that the CoolCalifornia City Challenge is not a harmless
contest; it is promoting a hoax known as global warming. She said that anything involving
sustainability is supporting U.N. Agenda 21. She wondered if it is data mining and personal
information will be going to private firms and she recommended that residents not register for
the challenge. Council Member Schlicht stated that she voted no on item 12 regarding the
closure of the Mission Viejo Foundation because the City Council gave $450,000 as seed money
to the foundation and the foundation's promises fell short. She doesn't feel that the City should
City Council Minutes  8  March 3, 2014
 close the books to remove the $102,000 shortfall until we have an explanation. Jim Leach, the
President at the time, promised to generate $1-1.5 million within 12 months and she believes that
he still owes an explanation to the residents as to how the $450,000 was spent. Council Member
Schlicht expressed that she was extremely fortunate to attend the American Legion Post 862 Law
and Order Awards ceremony because she was privileged to hear what turned out to be the last
prayers to God and Country by Pastor Tom Tyree. Mr. Tyree, who was Pastor to Post 862 for
many years, died the next day and she read the American Legion's announcement on his
passing. In honor of Pastor Tyree, Council Member Schlicht read a stanza from the Battle Hymn
of the Republic: "Mine eyes have seen the glory of the coming of the Lord; He is trampling out
the vintage where the grapes of wrath are stored; He hath loosed the fateful lightning of His
terrible swift sword; His truth is marching on."

Council Member Ury

Council Member Ury provided a reminder that Leigh Steinberg will be speaking in Mission
Viejo on March 6 at 7:00 p.m. at the Community Center and he encouraged residents to
attend. He also noted that people had a lot of fun with the rains over the last few days and there
are some interesting videos online of the water coming through the Youth Athletic Park, which is
also a flood control channel. Council Member Ury asked Mayor Kelley to adjourn tonight's
meeting in memory of a dear family friend, Dan Josiphovich.

Mayor Pro Tem Leckness

Mayor Pro Tem Leckness read notes from La Paz Intermediate School students who thanked him
for speaking about his role as a Council Member at the school's Career Day. He also discussed
his attendance at a junior high school Community of Character forum with moderator Russ
Williams. The students are given a scenario or challenge that they have to respond to and the
topic at the forum he attended was bullying. Mayor Pro Tem Leckness noted that bullying is a
huge problem which can also occur online and since kids don't want to tell their parents, the
adults often don't know it is happening. He also outlined his attendance at a recent Mission
Viejo Rotary Club meeting where a Grand Juror explained the job and announced that they are
seeking people to sit on the Orange County Grand Jury. Mr. Leckness stated that the one-year
commitment is a great opportunity for someone who is retired and he encouraged residents to
look into it if they are interested. He also thanked City Manager Wilberg for his recent
presentation to the Economic Coalition. He stated that other cities look to us to see how we are
doing things and he noted that we have to be aware of what is going on in neighboring
communities so that we can help to keep our businesses strong. Mayor Pro Tem Leckness
agreed with Council Member Schlicht that the Council asked staff to come back with library
attendance numbers and he said he would still like that information. He also discussed his recent
acquaintance with a resident who has the "greenest house in Mission Viejo." He visited the
family last week and he was very impressed with the home's efficiencies from solar tubes and
panels, to energy efficient appliances. Lastly, Mayor Pro Tem Leckness announced that there
will be a new community and bee garden at the corner of Marguerite Parkway and Medical
Center Road. He stated that it is the City's job to make this a great spot and will keep everyone
informed as the project unfolds.

City Council Minutes  9  March 3, 2014
 Mayor Kelley

Mayor Kelley notified her colleagues that she will be out of town March 7 through 15 while
helping her daughter and grandchildren out of state (she will be available by phone and
email.) She discussed her participation in the Los Alisos Intermediate School Character Forum,
a program that was rolled out this year by the Character Committee. Mayor Kelley noted that she
is one of the organizers of the event which is a presentation by facilitator Russ Williams who
lays out scenarios for 7th and 8th grade students to discuss and determine how they would react to
the situation. The program was previously held at Newhart Middle School and both Principals
wanted to focus on the issue of bullying or cyber-bullying. Mayor Kelley praised the table
mentors from the Chamber of Commerce as well as City Council Members and said she looks
forward to continuing the project because the Committee has received really good feedback from
the students themselves. Mayor Kelley recognized Orange County Register Report Chris Yee
who has faithfully attended every City Council meeting since he was appointed to Mission Viejo
in January. Mr. Yee is now going to be covering Pasadena so she said goodbye and thanked him
for keeping the public aware of what is going on in the community while he was here. Mayor
Kelley announced that the Community of Character word for the month is integrity and she
discussed the importance of character education in our schools. She noted that the character
movie this month is Mr. Holland's Opus and it will be screened on Sunday, March 9 from 2:00 to
4:50 p.m. in the Council Chamber. Mayor Kelley concluded with a reminder of the Lord of the
Strings concert featuring Laurence Juber, a two-time Grammy winner and former lead guitarist
for Paul McCartney's Wings. The concert will be held on Saturday, March 8 at 7:00 p.m. in the
Council Chamber and additional information is available online.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 9:58 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Kelley adjourned the meeting in memory of Tom Tyree and Dan Josiphovich, to Monday,
March 17, 2014, at 5:00 p.m.

______________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of March 17, 2014

City Council Minutes  10  March 3, 2014
